scope.task: Diagnose the 889.86-second PR-122 integration bottleneck and propose safe acceleration without editing production files or running the full suite.

verdict.summary: The dominant bottleneck is repeated full parsing and validation of the same CF4 quarantine policy while constructing each package entry, amplified by repeated payload and ZIP construction in the contract tests. Exhaustive repository scanning is the second hotspot. Git binary-binding subprocesses are measurable but secondary.

findings.statement: _entry_rows resolves a reviewed sidecar pin independently for every package entry; that helper reparses and fully validates the same YAML policy on every call.
evidence: scripts/build_external_audit_package.py:983-1026 loops over 555 entries and calls reviewed_active_binary_sidecar_pin at line 1013.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:2297-2318 shows that every helper call invokes load_policy at line 2314.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:547-560 reads and yaml.safe_load parses the policy; the remainder of load_policy validates paths, pins, sidecars, and artifact digests.
cProfile: build_audit_package_payload 88.806 s; _entry_rows 58.345 s; 559 load_policy calls 57.002 s; 564 yaml.safe_load calls 41.037 s.
Unprofiled baseline payload: 41.412723 s for 555 entries and 3268 scanned paths.
Process-local simulation of one validated policy snapshot for one build: 17.283692 s, with 559 call sites but one actual load; absolute saving 24.129031 s and relative saving 58.27%.
A second simulation covering payload plus build_zip_bytes took 33.614993 s: payload 17.563609 s and ZIP 16.051384 s, with 563 policy call sites and one actual load.
assumptions: The working tree remained unchanged during each isolated measurement.
The in-memory monkeypatch changed only repeated load_policy evaluation; it did not bypass source-byte, sidecar, Git HEAD, quarantine, or ZIP revalidation paths.
cProfile cumulative times have instrumentation overhead, so unprofiled timings are used for expected wall-time benefit.

findings.statement: Every payload performs an exhaustive repository quarantine validation, every ZIP build performs another, and the test module repeats both operations many times.
evidence: scripts/build_external_audit_package.py:1436-1476 revalidates all packaged bytes and calls assert_repository_clean once per ZIP build.
htt/src/common/cf4_p0_quarantine.py:2357-2453 enumerates and scans active repository paths; _repository_candidate_paths uses git ls-files at lines 1072-1099.
cProfile: validate_repository 24.631 s and _scan_text 6.211 s for one profiled payload.

Static call counting in tests/contracts/test_audit_package_generator.py finds 13 successful full payload constructions and 7 ZIP constructions: six _payload calls, one direct payload call, six CLI payloads, four direct/fixtureless ZIP builds, and three CLI ZIP builds. This implies 20 exhaustive validation passes in this test module.
The exact source-only --check observation supplied by the main writer was 41.99 s at 103% CPU and 183564 KiB RSS before reporting a stale manifest.
assumptions: The static count describes the successful paths in the current tests; early-failing negative payload tests were excluded because they do not reach repository validation.

findings.statement: Per-binary Git binding launches many subprocesses, but it is not the cause of the order-of-magnitude delay.
evidence: htt/src/common/package_binary_binding.py:133-166 invokes git rev-parse and git show for same-path HEAD byte checks; verify_package_binary_binding invokes this path at lines 402-449.
cProfile: 825 verify_package_binary_binding calls consumed 3.372 s; 1009 subprocess.run calls consumed 2.510 s; _repository_candidate_paths itself consumed 0.259 s.
assumptions: Git object data was warm enough for the measured run; cold storage could increase this component, but it remains below repeated YAML validation in the measured profile.

recommendations.option: Use one validated policy snapshot per package build
recommendations.expected_benefit: Measured payload reduction from 41.413 s to 17.284 s, saving 24.129 s or 58.3% per payload. With 13 payload constructions, the non-additive suite-level opportunity is roughly 250-315 s before test deduplication.
design: Load and fully validate policy bytes once at the package-build boundary and retain the returned policy hash.
Resolve reviewed_active_binary_sidecar pins from that immutable build-local mapping instead of calling load_policy per entry.
Pass the same snapshot explicitly to repository validation where practical, or at minimum compare the final validation policy_sha256 with the initial snapshot hash.
Re-read the small policy bytes at the final boundary and fail if the hash changed during the build; do not rely on mtime.
Retain verify_package_binary_binding and verify_packaged_entry_bytes re-reads, reviewed sidecar digest checks, Git HEAD authority checks, and final assert_repository_clean.
recommendations.forbidden_variant: Do not use a module-global or functools.lru_cache policy object; that could accept stale policy, sidecar, or artifact state across builds and tests.

recommendations.option: Share immutable payload and archive fixtures among pure assertion tests
recommendations.expected_benefit: Current-state ceiling: eliminating five of six repeated _payload calls saves about 207 s at the measured 41.4 s baseline; after the policy fix it still saves about 85 s. Reusing one deterministic archive for the two token-inspection tests while retaining one fresh comparison can remove roughly one to two 16 s ZIP builds after the policy fix.
design: Create a module-scoped immutable payload fixture only for tests that inspect the same worktree snapshot and do not mutate repository inputs.
Create one archive fixture for content/token assertions; retain a separate fresh build in the determinism test so byte-for-byte determinism is still exercised.
Keep CLI launcher tests, mutation/fail-closed tests, and time-of-check/time-of-use tests independent and fresh.
recommendations.guard: Never share the fixture across tests that mutate inputs, monkeypatch validators, or are meant to prove fresh CLI/source-only execution.

recommendations.option: Short-circuit --check when required output files are absent
recommendations.expected_benefit: Saves one full payload construction in test_cli_check_detects_missing_and_stale_outputs: about 41 s now or about 17 s after the policy fix.
design: Resolve and safely inspect output paths before payload construction in --check mode; return the existing terminal missing-output failure immediately when either output is absent.
Do not short-circuit a present output: fresh and stale outputs must still receive full payload and byte validation.
recommendations.gate_risk: Confirm that --check is allowed to report the first terminal failure rather than aggregate every unrelated repository finding.

recommendations.expected_benefit: At most a few seconds per package in the measured profile; lower priority than policy snapshotting and test deduplication.
design: Capture HEAD OID once, enumerate path-to-blob OIDs once with git ls-tree, and read required blobs through one git cat-file --batch process.
Preserve distinct same-path exact-byte and reachable-legacy-blob decisions and bind the snapshot to the captured HEAD OID.

recommendations.option: Pre-normalize policy path sets and compiled scan rules
recommendations.expected_benefit: Modest secondary CPU reduction; the profile attributed 10.123 s to _is_repository_exception and 9.014 s to _matches_policy_prefix cumulatively under profiling, overlapping the scan path.
design: Build immutable normalized exact-path sets, boundary-aware prefix objects, and compiled regexes once in the build-local policy view.
Keep sorted path traversal and sorted issue output unchanged.

details: The primary hotspot is duplicate work, so eliminating repeated policy parses and repeated package builds dominates parallel execution.
Threading yaml.safe_load or Python regex scans does not bypass the GIL and would add synchronization and snapshot-consistency complexity.

Process-parallel repository scanning can restore deterministic issue order by sorting normalized results, but it duplicates a large policy/context and competes for filesystem cache; only the profiled 6.211 s _scan_text component is clearly parallelizable.
Running these tests with multiple pytest workers would multiply exhaustive Git/filesystem scans and the measured approximately 184 MiB RSS, so it may be slower and substantially more memory hungry.
Parallel ZIP compression or entry emission is not recommended because exact archive bytes, fixed member ordering, and deterministic compression are gate inputs.
parallelism_assessment.conditional_option: After duplicate-work fixes, benchmark process-parallel text scanning only, with a frozen candidate-path/content-hash snapshot, stable sorted findings, identical mutation-corpus results, and unchanged ZIP bytes.

gpu_assessment.reason: The workload is YAML parsing, pathlib/stat/read operations, regex scanning, SHA-256, Git subprocesses, and deterministic DEFLATE. It has no dense numerical or array kernel; transfer and marshaling overhead would dominate and GPU libraries would enlarge the trusted/runtime surface.

python_vectorization_assessment.reason: NumPy-style vectorization does not fit heterogeneous path, YAML, regex, Git, and byte-validation control flow. hashlib and zlib already use optimized native implementations. Pre-normalizing path sets and compiling regexes is ordinary algorithmic preprocessing, not numerical vectorization, and is the only relevant Python-side micro-optimization after duplicate work is removed.

reproduction.command_summary: Import scripts/build_external_audit_package.py with importlib under venv/bin/python -B; call build_audit_package_payload once with fixed git_commit and worktree_state; measure with time.perf_counter.
Wrap the same single build_audit_package_payload call with cProfile.Profile, write /tmp/pr122_payload.prof, then inspect with pstats sorted by cumulative time.
reproduction.result: 230843377 calls in 88.806 s; _entry_rows 58.345 s; load_policy 57.002 s/559; yaml.safe_load 41.037 s/564; validate_repository 24.631 s; _scan_text 6.211 s; verify_package_binary_binding 3.372 s/825; subprocess.run 2.510 s/1009.

reproduction.command_summary: In one isolated Python process, monkeypatch common.cf4_p0_quarantine.load_policy with a dictionary keyed by resolved repo root and policy path; run exactly one payload build, retaining all other validators and byte checks.
Using the same build-local policy snapshot simulation, run one payload build followed by one build_zip_bytes call without writing outputs.
reproduction.result: payload=17.563609 zip=16.051384 total=33.614993 bytes=42249605 policy_calls=563 actual_loads=1

remaining_risks: The one-load simulation demonstrates performance, not implementation correctness; a production patch still needs mutation tests for policy, sidecar, binary, symlink, HEAD movement, and mid-build byte changes.
Suite-level savings are not exactly additive because filesystem/Git caches and cProfile overhead change marginal costs.
Do not remove the final source-byte and quarantine validation merely to gain speed; it closes the manifest-to-ZIP mutation window.
